thread:
Alex N: heads up — found a billing edgecase when customers move between regions mid-request. attribution keys collapse and VAT tags mismatch :grimace:
Samir: can you sketch the flow? is this when a request fans out to cross-region services?
Alex N: yep. scenario: tenant in eu-west starts a long streaming job, part of the job routed to us-east for capacity. usage events arrive with different region tags and the tenant's billing jur ids differ. we end up double-counting tokens during reconciliation.
Maria G: ouch. do we have an atomic provenance id across the whole request? last I checked prefix_fingerprint was per ingress region.
Alex N: currently the prefix_fingerprint is generated at the edge and includes region shard. so the same logical session has two distinct fingerprints.
Jon P: what about using a top-level request_id that we propagate in headers and through the fanout? we already do x-request-id for tracing.
Samir: we do, but not all downstream infra emits it into metering events. a few legacy connectors only emit local fingerprint.
Maria G: short term: add a join step in billing recon that dedups by (request_id OR token_fingerprint) and merge attribution. long term: enforce request_id propagation in contract.
Alex N: agreed. also VAT/jurisdiction — when region changes, tax rate should be determined by tenant billing profile, not event region. currently the tax calc runs at aggregation time using event.region which is wrong.
Jon P: so two fixes: 1) provenance canonicalization (best-effort merge of fingerprints) 2) tax jurisdiction override by tenant metadata at finalize.
Samir: merging fingerprints will be messy. what do we do with partial attributions? e.g., a single chat chunk consumed tokens from model A in eu-west and model B in us-east. who gets the charge?
Maria G: charges should be split by token counts per provider region but billed under tenant's jurisdiction. the ledger should keep per-provider usage rows and a single invoice-level jurisdiction field.
Alex N: implementation idea: add provenance envelope step that emits canonical_id and component rows: [{provider: "eu-west", tokens: 120}, {provider: "us-east", tokens: 80}] then billing pipeline consumes envelope -> creates per-provider line items + invoice-level tax computed from tenant metadata.
Samir: sounds good. we need to be careful about late-arriving component rows (streaming continues after close). we already have late-arrival windowing; need to run reconciliation to patch invoice lines and emit audit events.
Jon P: audit event model: include original_envelope_id, reconciled_flag, delta_tokens. emit to audit log and to customer observability.
Maria G: and add a metric for "jurisdiction_override_count" so finance can see how often events had mismatched regions.
Samir: quick prototype: patch ingest to copy x-request-id into metering.events.request_id, and add an optional canonical_id header if edge sees multi-shard. then add compact-reconciler job to merge.
Alex N: can someone pick up the RFC follow-up? I'll volunteer to write the envelope schema. cc @Samir for the recon job and @Maria G for billing rules.
Samir: I'll start a PR for request_id propagation and a small converter for legacy connectors.
Maria G: I'll draft billing rule changes and VAT override docs.
MeteringBot: deploy-bot: metering-ingest v2 deployed to canary (eu-west) at 2026-03-21T15:12:03Z :rocket:
Alex N: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 11am to review envelope schema and recon retry strategy. :thumbsup:
